Hospital RCM Consulting

Diagnosing the Revenue Cycle Before Prescribing a Fix

Hospitals and multi-provider health systems run revenue cycles at a scale where the smallest inefficiency compounds fast. A department-level coding gap, an outdated fee schedule, or an under-resourced A/R team does not just cost one claim, it costs thousands of them across every provider using the same broken process.

PMEX's hospital RCM consulting starts with a full assessment of the existing revenue cycle: workflow by workflow, department by department, to find exactly where coding and billing improvements will have the biggest financial impact. From there, our consultants design targeted solutions instead of a generic fix, because a radiology department's revenue leaks are rarely the same as a surgical department's.

The engagement treats the revenue cycle as a whole system, not a series of isolated problems, so the fixes we prescribe strengthen the entire operation rather than moving the same bottleneck somewhere else.

Where Hospitals Lose Revenue

The Six Areas Our Assessments Focus On

Department Coding Variance

Different coding accuracy and specificity between departments using the same payer contracts.

Denial Concentration

A small number of departments or procedures usually drive most of the denial volume.

A/R Backlog Concentration

Aging balances often cluster in specific service lines with thinner follow-up resources.

Contract Underperformance

Payer contracts that have not been renegotiated in years, paying below current market rates.

Staffing Misalignment

Billing and coding staff spread too thin, or misaligned to where claim volume actually sits.

Outdated Technology

Legacy systems that cannot support automated scrubbing or real-time reporting.
